thread:
tara: quick sync: I prototyped a different angle on schema gating + billing propagation. instead of a single giant migration, we add a lightweight compatibility adapter layer at the ingest boundary.

ben: can you sketch the adapter responsibilities? sounds promising if it's low-risk.

tara: adapter responsibilities: normalize incoming fields -> canonical attribute names, validate billing keys, emit 'schema_version' header, and optionally enrich missing billing info from lookup service. important: adapters must be idempotent and cheap.

hema: how do we avoid double-enrichment causing cost attribution drift? past attempts introduced racey backfills and inflated billed spans.

tara: two parts: 1) adapters never mutate raw envelope -- they emit derived attributes into the envelope.metadata section so downstream can decide what to trust, 2) we add an attribution_confidence score (0..100) attached to the billing_key to drive billing heuristics.

jon: attribution_confidence is interesting. what's the lifecycle? do we recompute later in batch jobs?

tara: yes. streaming assigns a best-effort confidence; analytics recomputes definitive key and writes overrides to a small reconciliation table. query/billing jobs consult reconciliation table with prefer_streaming=false by default. we expose a feature-flag to let tenants opt into 'billing-from-stream' if they want lowest-latency attribution.

ben: we need to be careful about TTL and stale reconciliation entries. how long do we keep reconciliation overrides?

tara: default 7 days, configurable per-tenant. rationale: most reclassification happens within a day. long-tail legal corrections are rare and handled by manual reclassification job.

schema-lint-bot: schema-lint: incoming patch requires adding new top-level attribute 'effective_billing_key' to trace envelope. please follow attribute naming conventions: snake_case, <=64 chars, and register in registry.

hema: registry changes are friction. can we use dynamic registration for adapters so teams don't need PRs for every new attribute?

tara: dynamic registration is fine for experimental attrs; but anything that affects cost/billing must go through registry PR + audit. we need an audit trail.

jon: what about contract versioning in the ingest API? we should avoid heavy-weight deploy-time checks. suggest we support a version header and default to v1 until tenant flips to v2. adapters can honor version header.

ben: rollout plan sketch: 1) implement adapter shim behind feature flag, 2) enable for internal tenants only, 3) run streaming vs batch diff job to measure attribution divergence, 4) open registry PRs for any canonical attrs we introduce, 5) slowly open to customers.

hema: one more operational concern: memory and QPS of the billing lookup service. if adapter calls lookup in the hot path we'll add latency. can we use a best-effort LRU cache with async refresh?

tara: yep. adapter consults local LRU cache first. on miss, adapter emits envelope with provisional 'billing_lookup_pending' flag and schedules async resolution. when async result arrives, reconciliation table is written and downstream reclassification job can re-emit corrected events if necessary.

jon: nice. monitoring/alerting: track 'provisional_billing_fraction', 'reconciliation_lag_p95', and 'billing_mismatch_rate' between streaming and batch. set pager if mismatch_rate > 0.2% for > 15m.

ben: and add a console page listing 'inferred' vs 'canonical' keys for a sample of traces per tenant. UX requested that to debug customer tickets.

hema: edge-case: what if adapter enrichment leaks PII into derived attrs? we need to ensure PII redaction rules apply to derived metadata too.

tara: agreed. adapter must run redaction pipeline identical to ingest preprocessor. and derived attributes flagged as 'sensitive' are stored in encrypted metadata and not shown in console unless tenant has permission.

schema-lint-bot: note: remember to update agents/docs: schema-registry playbook with steps for billing attr PR and emergency rollback procedure.

jon: next steps: tara will write RFC with adapter API, attribute schema additions, reconciliation flow, and monitoring. hema to review security/PII section and ben to detail UX console mockups. target: RFC by next Tue, prototype in staging by end of sprint.

ben: one last thought: consider a sandbox listener that replays streaming canonicalization logic into a side queue so we can run A/B diffs with zero risk to main billing pipelines. helps prove correctness before touching billing.

tara: love that. I'll add a 'shadow-canonicalizer' to the RFC. thanks all. :rocket:
